title: Evidence index for the Nested Resonance Memory archive
description: Every number the README gives in digits, as claims with a status and the committed file that holds each number. The Nested Resonance Memory hypothesis is open: no claim here establishes it.
author: Aldrin Payopay

rule.normalize: every run of whitespace becomes one space, and every '*' and '`' is deleted
rule.needle: a needle is a verbatim excerpt of its evidence file; it matches when its normalized text is a substring of the normalized file
rule.number: a quoted number is found when its value (thousands commas and a trailing % removed) is a number token inside a matching needle; dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and fractions (1/20) must appear literally
rule.coverage: every number written in digits in README prose (code, link targets, URLs, HTML tags and list markers are not prose) lies inside exactly one claim's or non-claim's quote
rule.quote: each quote occurs exactly once in README.md, and its numbers are exactly the digits inside it
rule.tracked: every evidence file is tracked by git, so a fresh clone has it
rule.words: numbers written as words are indexed by hand where they carry a result; they are not machine-counted

statuses.established: a measured number or fact that the cited file holds, stated within that file's own scope
statuses.qualified: holds only inside the scope written beside it; quote the scope with the claim
statuses.open: a question the archive has not decided; the hypothesis itself is open
statuses.retired: a claim the archive has withdrawn; the evidence names the file that withdrew it; do not cite it as current

kinds.measurement: a number measured from runs or records
kinds.instrument: what the instrument does or records
kinds.software: what a tool or library does, with its tests
kinds.procedure: a step a reader can run
kinds.historical-count: a count of past work, not a count of validations
kinds.hypothesis: a proposition under test; always open
kinds.label: a name or pointer, such as a ring number in a link

terms.F1-F5: the memory estimator's five pre-declared tests; F1 is labelled a check, F2-F5 falsifiers (F3 injected-effect recovery, F4 robustness across alternative settings, F5 at least three measurable conditions)
terms.E1-E5b: the estimator's eligibility gates for a run-epoch; E5b is the seed-balance gate
terms.V1-V5: Ring 30's gates, checked before its decision rule is read
terms.L and Pi frames: Ring 30 scores each run as recorded (L, the lab frame) and with its inversions undone (Pi)
terms.invert_all / invert_matter: Ring 30's arms: everything inverted through the chamber's centre (the positive control), or only the matter (the decided arm)
terms.monopole: the spherically symmetric part of a field, removed before scoring
terms.effective cells: a participation ratio: how many cells effectively carry a pattern
terms.sim_digest: a hash over the page's GPU program, named physics constants and drive; runs with the same digest ran the same simulation
